comment_purpose: What Git Crafter publishes, and where. Keys under files are paths relative to the Git Crafter root. Values are paths relative to the target. Declaring a target here writes nothing. Only claude_os_sync.py apply --yes writes, and only to the paths listed. It lists only user-claude. Another repo vendors a copy of the file it needs, with first lines naming its Git Crafter path and commit SHA.
comment_path: Each path is the repo's main checkout, so apply writes into whatever branch that checkout has out. To target a git worktree instead, such as <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>, pass --repo-path PATH with one repo name, for status, diff, plan or apply. The record file goes there too. Apply prints the target branch, and refuses a checkout with staged or unstaged changes to tracked files unless --force-target. Sources always come from the Git Crafter root, wherever this manifest lives.
comment_overlay: Each account's own facts are not in Git Crafter. They live in that account's private overlay folder, laid out like ~/.claude (code-os/account.json from config/account.example.json, code-os/claude_deny.local.json for deny rules that fit only that account, and any rules/<name>.md of its own), installed with apply user-claude --yes --overlay DIR. Only code-os/ and rules/ are taken, an overlay never replaces a file listed here, and it installs only once merged in its own checkout. Without an overlay, the rules that read account.json fall back to asking the owner.
comment_user_claude: user-claude installs tier 1 into ~/.claude for this account: the rules, the merging skill, claude_deny.py with its model and the claude_deny.json permissions.deny list it merges into settings.json, the two hookify rules, the Comfy guard, voice_lint.py, and json_facts.py, which reads facts from ~/.claude.json, a file the Read(~/.claude.json) deny rule keeps from every other read. Apply never edits settings.json: after an apply that changes claude_deny.json, run python3 -I ~/.claude/code-os/claude_deny.py --merge ~/.claude/settings.json --yes, and wire the Comfy guard by hand from the entry in its header. The hookify plugin loads hookify.*.local.md from .claude/ under a session's working folder, so the two installed in ~/.claude/ fire in sessions run from the home folder; Git Crafter's own .claude/ copies fire in its sessions. Hookify rules fire in sessions under the home folder; a project session elsewhere relies on Claude Code's built-in critical-path check, which blocks a recursive delete of the home folder, glob and trailing-slash forms included, in every folder and permission mode (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions and /permission-modes, read 2026-11-23). ~/.claude is not a git checkout, so apply warns and writes. Apply only copies: a file dropped from this list stays installed until someone deletes it by hand. It copies, never symlinks: a plugin cannot ship rules (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components, read 2026-11-02), and Cowork skips a symlinked rules folder that points outside the working directory (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, read 2026-11-02).
